official.application_route: Apply first to a Swedish master's programme through University Admissions, then submit one digital application in SI's own portal during the February window.
official.citizenship_residency: Must be a citizen of one of the 34 eligible countries; residency in that country at the time of application is not required, and SI does not consider the applicant's current country of residence when selecting.
official.international_eligibility: Open only to citizens of the 34 listed countries; Swedish and EU/EEA citizens, holders of Swedish permanent residence permits, and holders of work- or family-based residence permits tied to Swedish or EU/EEA citizens are excluded.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The programme must appear on SI's published list of eligible English-taught master's programmes; supported fields of study are governance, public health, entrepreneurship and innovation, and STEM.
official.duration: Full-time, one- or two-year master's programme beginning in the autumn semester
official.description: SI describes the scholarship as a competitive, fully funded award for global professionals from 34 eligible countries who want to contribute to the sustainable development of their home country, offering world-class education, cutting-edge research and a network of peers while developing the tools to drive change back home.
official.program_type: Government scholarship (Swedish Institute public agency), master's level
official.english_requirement: SI states it has no language proficiency or GPA requirements of its own at master's level; these assessments are made by the universities and University Admissions, so English requirements follow each university's rules.

verification.notes: The SEK 12,000 monthly amount, the SEK 15,000 travel grant (SEK 10,000 for six countries), full tuition payment and the exclusions were all read directly from SI's own programme page; application documents, template rules and reference-letter rules were confirmed on SI's FAQ. No aggregator was used.

applicant_utility.summary: This is SI's flagship fully funded master's award: tuition is paid straight to your university while you receive SEK 12,000 per month plus a one-time travel grant, so the money question is settled before you fly. The work is front-loaded, though - you must already hold a Swedish admission offer on the results day, which means the University Admissions deadline in January effectively gates the scholarship. Practically, that gives you a three-month gap between the two applications, so treat January as the real deadline and use February only to refine the scholarship file.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Professionals aged roughly 26-40 from the 34 eligible countries with 3,000+ certified work hours, at least one signed leadership role, and a credible story about what they will change at home after graduating.
application_readiness_checklist: Start the University Admissions application in October, not January - pay the SEK application fee on time because SI cannot consider you otherwise
Download SI's document templates only from the mid-November publication; SI re-issues the forms each year and last year's version is invalid

Get work and leadership experience certified on SI's own form, signed and stamped by someone who knows you professionally (HR, head of organisation, or for freelancers the agency you're registered with)
Brief both referees in advance: SI contacts them directly and needs them to answer email, including spam folders, until the announcement
Draft the motivation letter as an explicit country-development argument, naming the SDG or sector your programme serves rather than listing personal ambitions
Confirm your chosen programme is still on the current eligible-programmes PDF before you submit
common_rejection_risks: Applying late to University Admissions so you are not admitted on the first results day - SI states it can make no exception
Submitting a CV in any other format, including Europass, or more than three pages - SI disqualifies these outright
Uploading a previous year's template or an unsigned/unstamped experience form
Using dual citizenship to submit more than one application, which disqualishes all of them
Failing to reach 3,000 provable hours across no more than three employers (internships do not count)
Being admitted only as a reserve or in the late round, neither of which is fundable
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The University Admissions application fee, which SI explicitly does not cover and which is not refundable; insurance, since SI's scholarship contains no insurance cover at all; travel and living costs beyond the SEK 12,000 monthly allowance and the one-time grant; and any costs for family members, for whom SI provides no additional grant.
document_audit: Work experience forms must come first in the merged PDF in reverse chronological order, followed by leadership forms in reverse chronological order, capped at five pages total excluding the instruction page
Each individual work or leadership form may not exceed one page

Reference letters must be signed by someone who knows you professionally, not personally; if the letter is translated, only a notarised translator may do it and the original plus translation must be one PDF
The CV is limited to three pages on the SI template with no annexes, so publications and achievement evidence cannot be attached there
Use a PC rather than a Mac when completing the forms if the dropdown fields do not open
alerts: The portal closes at 14:59 CET on the final day, not at midnight - a two-week window total
The scholarship cannot be transferred to a different programme or extended beyond the awarded study period
SI will not help you negotiate leave of absence with your employer; arrange that before you apply
Deferral is only possible after your studies have started
The eligible country list is reviewed against SI's government directives and has changed before, so re-check it in mid-November rather than assuming last year's list still holds
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Two separate systems: University Admissions first (open October, closing mid-January), then SI's own portal in February, where a single application covers both the Global Professionals and Pioneering Women in STEM awards - you cannot submit two SI applications.

benefits: Travelling expenses for the least expensive fare from your residential address in Sweden, Finland, Denmark or Iceland to Uppsala and return
Free accommodation centrally located in Uppsala for the one-month stay
A subsistence allowance of SEK 450 per day
A desk and computer in a shared office at the Institute for the duration of the stay
Access to the Nordic Africa Institute's library collections on contemporary Africa - books, periodicals, newspapers and government publications
Support to connect to existing work at the Institute through NAI research hosts
eligibility: You must be pursuing Africa-oriented studies or research within the fields of social sciences or humanities
You can be a master student, PhD candidate, postdoctoral or mid-career researcher

You may apply regardless of citizenship, but you must be affiliated to and based at a university or research centre in Sweden, Finland, Denmark or Iceland, both when you apply and when you take up the scholarship
The scholarship is awarded for a one-month stay at the Nordic Africa Institute in Uppsala
Persons currently or previously employed by, or otherwise professionally affiliated with, the Nordic Africa Institute are not eligible
requirements: The application and all appendices must be in English
Incomplete applications will not be considered
The application must be uploaded with all four listed documents
documents: Up-to-date CV including a list of publications, if any

Outline of the research project, 3-5 pages, covering the objective of the research project with the topic clearly identified and contextualised within its academic discipline, the method and time frame including research method, data-gathering techniques and time frame, and a brief theoretical explication
Work plan, 1 page, specific to the time spent at the Institute, clarifying what part of the research project will be worked on during the stay
Reference - a signed letter of support from the applicant's supervisor or head of department confirming current affiliation and field of research
selection_criteria: Applications are primarily evaluated on the outline of the research project
A selection committee is formed for each announcement and assesses applications under transparent rules of ethics and proficiency
The committee weighs how clearly the applicant's own framing and academic positioning of the research comes through
coverage: Travel at the least expensive fare from the residential address in Sweden, Finland, Denmark or Iceland to Uppsala and return
Free accommodation centrally located in Uppsala
Subsistence allowance of SEK 450 per day
Workspace, computer and library access during the one-month stay
application_method: Open the 'Apply for the Nordic Scholarship Programme 2027' link on the Nordic Africa Institute opportunities page, which points to NAI's online application form
Register and complete the online application
Upload the up-to-date CV including the list of publications
Upload the 3-5 page outline of the research project
Upload the 1-page work plan specific to the stay at the Institute
Upload the signed letter of support from your supervisor or head of department

official.application_route: One online application via the form linked from NAI's Nordic Scholarship Programme page, with all four documents uploaded in English as appendices.
official.citizenship_residency: No citizenship restriction is published; applicants may apply regardless of citizenship but must be affiliated to and based at a university or research centre in Sweden, Finland, Denmark or Iceland.
official.international_eligibility: Open to applicants of any nationality, provided they are based at a university or research centre in Sweden, Finland, Denmark or Iceland; the scheme is not restricted to citizens of those countries, but applicants outside them are not eligible.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Africa-oriented studies or research in the social sciences or humanities.
official.research_requirement: A 3-5 page research project outline and a 1-page work plan for the stay are mandatory, and applications are primarily evaluated on the research outline.
official.duration: One-month stay at the Nordic Africa Institute in Uppsala
official.description: NAI describes the programme as a way to build capacity in the production of knowledge about Africa and to promote and establish relations with and between Nordic research communities, offering a one-month stay at the Institute so that researchers can use its collections on contemporary Africa and connect to work at the Institute through NAI research hosts.
official.program_type: Research funding - short-term visiting scholarship, one month, awarded once per year
official.english_requirement: The application and all appendices must be in English.

not_confirmed: Number of scholarships awarded per round (NAI does not publish it)
Exact dates or scheduling of the one-month stay
Any tuition figure - NAI publishes none, as this is a visiting research stay rather than a degree programme
verification.notes: The SEK 450 per day subsistence allowance, the least-expensive-fare travel cover, free centrally located accommodation, the desk and computer, the four required documents and the 11 October 2026 closing date were all read directly from NAI's own programme page; the evaluation of proposals on the research outline was confirmed on the same page and the committee structure on NAI's selection-process page.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a one-month residency rather than a degree scholarship: you get a desk, free accommodation in central Uppsala, SEK 450 a day and a return fare to Nordic-based researchers working on Africa in the social sciences or humanities. The strength of your application is almost entirely the research outline, and NAI says it reads proposals carefully and wants to hear your research in your own words - so a polished but borrowed text actively costs you marks. Note the current round closes on 11 October 2026, the day after this record was verified, so the next window is the following autumn.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Doctoral students and postdocs in the Nordics whose Africa-focused project needs NAI's unique government publications and newspaper holdings, and who can name a specific piece of writing they will finish in Uppsala.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your supervisor will sign the reference letter well before 11 October - it must state both your current affiliation and your field of research
Rewrite the research outline specifically for this stay, with a one-page work plan that names which section or dataset the Uppsala month will actually produce
Check your page budget: the outline must be 3-5 pages, the work plan exactly 1 page, with no room for padding
Contact Marie Karlsson at NAI (marie.karlsson@nai.uu.se) only after reading the page, since her office handles the programme directly
common_rejection_risks: Submitting an incomplete application - NAI states incomplete applications will not be considered, with no chance to top them up
Losing the Nordic-base requirement by moving institutions between applying and taking up the scholarship
Being currently or previously employed by, or professionally affiliated with, the Nordic Africa Institute
A work plan that reads as generic and could be executed anywhere, rather than tied to the Institute's collections and research hosts
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Insurance of any kind, since NAI states plainly that the scholarship does not include health care insurance or other insurances; daily expenses beyond SEK 450; any travel component more expensive than the least expensive fare, which NAI will not reimburse; and any costs for accompanying family members.
document_audit: Everything, including appendices, must be in English
The reference letter must be signed, not typed or drafted by you, and must confirm affiliation and field of research
The CV must be up to date and include a publication list even if short - an empty publications section is acceptable, a missing one is not
The research outline is graded primarily, so its objective, method and time frame, and theoretical explication sections must each be explicitly labelled
alerts: The 2027 round closes 11 October 2026 - only one day after this record was verified, so treat it as effectively immediate
NAI warns that using AI to develop your text may place you at a disadvantage in the assessment
No insurance is included, so arrange your own cover for the month
NAI reserves the right to inform applicants that the programme cannot be implemented in 2027 if funding falls short
Scholarships are awarded only once per year, so missing this round means waiting for the next autumn call
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Single online submission through NAI's application form with all four documents attached; outcomes are communicated once the selection process is finalised and no later than the end of November 2026.
